description: For which real x is floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k maximal, and what is the maximal value?
guidelines: The correct answer is: maximum value is -1 + sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, achieved for all x in the union over integers m of [m + 1 - 1/n, m + 1).
0 points for conjecturing the maximum value or the optimal intervals without any proof.
0 points for computing f(x) for small specific values of n without generalizing the algebraic step.
0 points for restating the problem in an equivalent form without making any tangible progress toward bounding the sum.

children.description: Proves that f(x) is periodic with period 1 (i.e., f(x+1) = f(x)), allowing the domain to be restricted WLOG to an interval of length 1 such as [0,1).
Shows that f(x) is non-increasing on each interval [ℓ/n, (ℓ+1)/n) for integer ℓ, thereby restricting the search for the maximum to points of the form x = ℓ/n.
Observes that floor(nx) is constant on [ℓ/n, (ℓ+1)/n).
Observes that -sum floor(kx)/k can only decrease as x increases within such an interval, so f is non-increasing there.
Evaluates f(x) for the optimal range (e.g., x in [1-1/n, 1) or x = (n-1)/n) and explicitly computes the candidate maximum value -1 + sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.

scale.criterion: The candidate maximum value -1 + sum_{k=1}^n 1/k is correctly computed with no arithmetic errors.
The evaluation contains a minor arithmetic or off-by-one slip in the sum bounds or final value, despite otherwise correct reasoning for this step.

children.description: Expresses f(ℓ/n) algebraically in terms of fractional parts, deriving the identity f(ℓ/n) = sum_{k=1}^n {kℓ/n}/k (or an equivalent fractional-part reformulation).
Proves the general upper bound sum_{k=1}^n {kℓ/n}/k ≤ sum_{k=1}^n (n-k)/(nk) for all integers ℓ.
Proves the upper bound in full generality, correctly handling both the coprime case gcd(ℓ,n)=1 and the case gcd(ℓ,n)>1.
children.selection_signal: Solution proves the bound for all integers ℓ, with a rigorous argument covering gcd(ℓ,n)>1 (not merely asserting it follows from the coprime case).

children.description: Proves the upper bound only for the coprime case gcd(ℓ,n)=1, or claims the gcd>1 case follows trivially from the coprime case without proof.
children.selection_signal: Solution proves the bound when gcd(ℓ,n)=1 (e.g., via rearrangement inequality on the permuted fractional parts) but does not rigorously handle gcd(ℓ,n)>1, or assumes without proof that the gcd>1 case is majorized by the coprime case.

children.description: No meaningful progress toward proving the upper bound.
children.selection_signal: Solution does not prove or seriously attempt the upper bound in any case.

children.description: Identifies the correct equality cases of the upper bound and concludes that the maximum is achieved for exactly x in the union over integers m of [m + 1 - 1/n, m + 1).
